title: Derived pullback computes on resolving complexes with independent universes
statement: Let f be a ringed-topos pullback between independently sized essentially small sites, with coefficients in a common independent universe. Let (L, epsilon) be its complex-level universal left-derived pair. For every K-flat complex P with flat terms, epsilon at P is invertible. No equality of site universes, no flatness of the structural ring map, and no boundedness is assumed.

proof.text: The underlying-sheaf functor preserves finite limits and epimorphisms. Transfer these properties across the algebraic inverse-image comparison. Thus algebraic inverse image preserves homology. For the identity coefficient map, construct scalar extension and its inverse by the sheafification counit and multiplication; the balanced tensor identity identifies it naturally with the identity. Transport K-flatness through this isomorphism and apply preservation of the resolving class to deduce K-flatness after algebraic inverse image.

Factor ordinary pullback through algebraic inverse image followed by the prescribed scalar extension. The independent-coefficient scalar-extension theorem inverts quasi-isomorphisms between the K-flat images. The object and map presentation equalities give a natural isomorphism from the supplied ordinary pullback to this factorization, so it too inverts quasi-isomorphisms between resolving complexes.

Descend the supplied counit through the homotopy quotient, retaining its components. Every homotopy object admits a resolving complex. Apply the resolving-class left-derived theorem and identify its universal pair with the supplied pair by Kan-extension uniqueness. Its counit is invertible on the resolving class; the comparison isomorphism transfers that invertibility to the original counit.
